findings.what: The Why opens with "Still there.", a fragment that means nothing in a read-through; cut it or say what still holds ("The star rule still holds.").

findings.where: Screens 5, 7 and 9 (readouts while the fault on L1 slides) and screen 10's Why
findings.what: At 10 kΩ and 3 kΩ on L1 the readouts show L2 lowest (236 V and 211 V) while L1 still reads 253 V and 244 V, and no sentence explains it; screen 10 then finds the fault by the lowest line and the practice warns "do not assume the lowest line is the faulted one" with no reason, so add one sentence on screen 9 (with a high-resistance fault the line after the faulted one can read lowest; on 440 V a healthy line never drops below about 209 V on this curve, so 82 V must be the faulted line).

The screen's own demonstration already slides the fault from Open to Solid, so "Drag the fault on L1 from Open to Solid" asks him to repeat what he just watched; say "Watch the fault go from Open to Solid, then drag it back and try it."

The brief promised an insulation-rating bar and the rule that an insulated system's insulation is rated for the line voltage to earth (equipment at about 173% of phase voltage); neither is on any screen, and screen 7 stops at "1.73 times as much" without the design consequence.
"L2 sits most of the way to earth" is awkward; lead with the reading ("L2 reads far lowest, at 82 V, so the fault is on L2").
The picture and readouts show L1 and L2 at 440 V while the right answer is 400 V, with nothing saying the picture stays on its 440 V supply; add that to the Why or the feedback.
"drawn as in three-phase work" is vague; say what it is ("drawn as a phasor star").

findings.where: Screens 5, 7 and 9, the drawing near Solid
findings.what: Near Solid on L1 the earth dot rides on the motor's horizontal L1 feed wire (at 100 Ω it is within 2 px of it), so it can read as the hull touching the motor feed; run that wire from above the tip or move the card.

The opening screen is static, the earth dot that later moves is not drawn yet, and an empty band of about 130 px sits under the star where the key goes on later screens; grow the star in or trim the drawing when no key is shown.
The fifth tile, "Motor, L1 to L2", sits alone on its row and wraps "L2" onto a line of its own; a shorter label ("Motor, L1–L2") keeps it on one line.
